### Source 1: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC2880329

*   **Bibliographic Metadata:**
    *   **Title:** Simpson's paradox and experimental research (Source: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC2880329)
    *   **Authors:** Suzanne Ameringer, Ronald C. Serlin, Sandra Ward (Source: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC2880329)
    *   **Journal:** *Nursing Research* (Source: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC2880329)
    *   **Publication Date:** March-April 2009 (Source: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC2880329)
    *   **Volume/Issue/Pages:** Vol. 58, Issue 2, pp. 123–127 (Source: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC2880329)
    *   **Identifiers:** DOI: 10.1097/NNR.0b013e318199b517; PMID: 19289933; PMCID: PMC2880329 (Source: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC2880329)
*   **Study Design:** A methodological review and discussion paper. The aims of the paper were to describe Simpson's paradox, provide a hypothetical example, and discuss approaches to avoiding the paradox in experimental research (Source: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC2880329).
*   **Population:** Not applicable. This is a theoretical and methodological paper focused on experimental research in nursing rather than an empirical study involving a specific patient or participant population (Source: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC2880329).
*   **Interventions:** Not applicable. The paper discusses experimental interventions in a theoretical context, focusing on how confounding variables can distort the perceived effects of an intervention (Source: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC2880329).
*   **Outcomes:** The paper evaluates the threat of Simpson's paradox to internal validity and explores how it can lead to erroneous conclusions about the effects of experimental interventions (Source: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC2880329).
*   **Findings:** Simpson's paradox is a case of extreme confounding caused by an overlooked confounding variable that is disproportionately allocated among experimental groups. This can lead to an inference about an intervention effect that is the exact opposite of the correct conclusion. The paradox can be avoided by selecting appropriate experimental designs and analysis approaches that incorporate the confounding variable to obtain unconfounded estimates of treatment effects (Source: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC2880329).
*   **Limitations:** The paper relies on a hypothetical example and theoretical discussion rather than empirical data analysis from a specific clinical or experimental study (Source: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC2880329).

### Source 2: https://www.sciencedirect.com/topics/mathematics/length-sepal

*   **Bibliographic Metadata:**
    *   **Topic:** Length-sepal (Source: https://www.sciencedirect.com/topics/mathematics/length-sepal)
    *   **Platform/Section:** ScienceDirect Topics / Mathematics (Source: https://www.sciencedirect.com/topics/mathematics/length-sepal)
*   **Study Design:** Not a primary research study. It is a conceptual overview explaining data science and mathematical concepts, using the "Iris dataset" as a reference to explain distance metrics (Source: https://www.sciencedirect.com/topics/mathematics/length-sepal).
*   **Population:** Not applicable (Source: https://www.sciencedirect.com/topics/mathematics/length-sepal).
*   **Interventions:** Not applicable (Source: https://www.sciencedirect.com/topics/mathematics/length-sepal).
*   **Outcomes:** Not applicable (Source: https://www.sciencedirect.com/topics/mathematics/length-sepal).
*   **Findings:** The text explains that in datasets with heterogeneous attributes and varied units (e.g., credit scores and income), distance measures like Euclidean distance can be misleading because they depend heavily on the scale and units of the attributes. A small change in an attribute with a large scale (like income) might dominate the distance calculation compared to a large change in an attribute with a small scale (like credit score) (Source: https://www.sciencedirect.com/topics/mathematics/length-sepal).
*   **Limitations:** The conceptual limitation highlighted is that distance-based mathematical methods are inherently sensitive to the scale and units of input features, which can distort similarity measurements in practical datasets unless normalized or adjusted (Source: https://www.sciencedirect.com/topics/mathematics/length-sepal).
